articles.title: Arch Manning surpassed in 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings by rising superstar
articles.standfirst: The Texas Longhorns quarterback is no longer the consensus No. 1 overall pick many thought he would be.
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns quarterback is no longer the consensus No. 1 overall pick many thought he would be.
articles.body:
The 2025 college football season came with a bit of a shock to many: The consensus top team in the nation, the Texas Longhorns , stumbled out of the gate and couldn't recover in time to make the College Football Playoff .

In tune with that, Arch Manning had an inconsistent season that ended with more questions than answers about his football future. He was the Heisman Trophy favorite coming into the season, which was followed by an offseason in which many wondered if he should declare for the 2026 NFL Draft despite his up-and-down year.

Manning decided to play it safe and return to school for at least one more season. This upcoming year will be a crucial one for Manning's NFL future. A strong final season with the Longhorns could see him become the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft .

Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr considered strong contender to be No. 1 pick in 2027 NFL Draft

Right now, that isn't a given. In fact, there's another rising star quarterback in college football who has positioned himself ahead of Manning in the eyes of ESPN draft analyst Jordan Reid : Notre Dame's CJ Carr .

He now enters a pivotal season with heightened expectations. At 6-foot-2 and 215 pounds, Carr is an even-keeled distributor with enough arm strength to make things happen, and his feet and eyes are routinely tied together. He'll be the focal point of the Fighting Irish offense after they lost two first-round running backs. If he flourishes with that new responsibility, it's easy to see him being one of the first passers picked next April. "To be so young, I love how well he sees the field," an AFC assistant GM said. "I don't think he has the physical gifts of some others in this group, but I can easily see him jumping all of them because of his processing ability."

Reid technically has Carr in the same tier (Round 1) as Manning . Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Oregon's Dante Moore are also considered Round 1 guys. But Carr's 2026 season with the Fighting Irish has vaulted him to the top, at least for now.

Carr won the starting quarterback job before last season, but didn't make the impact he wanted through the first two games - both losses by Notre Dame. After that, it was smooth sailing for Carr and the Fighting Irish. Notre Dame won their final 10 games, and Carr threw for 2,741 yards, totaled 27 touchdowns and only threw six interceptions .

articles.title: Coach Prime Tax? Colorado player claims that playing for Deion Sanders is harming him and accuses the NCAA of foul play
articles.standfirst: Ezra Christensen is still waiting for a decision on his eligibility as the Colorado transfer argues that he is losing valuable preparation time ahead of the 2026 season
articles.summary: Ezra Christensen is still waiting for a decision on his eligibility as the Colorado transfer argues that he is losing valuable preparation time ahead of the 2026 season
articles.body:
E zra Christensen 's move to Colorado was supposed to be the next step in a remarkable football journey.

Instead, the defensive lineman has found himself watching the start of the season approach from the sidelines while his eligibility remains tied up in court.

Christensen transferred to the Buffaloes after an impressive 2025 season at New Mexico State, where he earned first-team All-Conference USA recognition after recording 42 tackles, 11 tackles for loss and six sacks.

Pro Football Focus also gave him an 88.6 overall grade, placing him among the country's most highly regarded interior defensive linemen.

Yet his place on Deion Sanders ' roster remains uncertain because of a dispute over whether he should receive another season of college eligibility.

Christensen has taken his fight against the NCAA to court, seeking an injunction that would allow him to play for Colorado during the 2026 campaign.

The dispute stems from the NCAA's eligibility rules and the way his previous seasons, including his time at junior college, have been counted.

For Christensen , the delay has become increasingly difficult to accept.

Speaking to DNVR, he suggested that the profile of his new program could be contributing to the complications.

“It’s frustrating to talk about it,” Ezra Christensen confessed. “I don’t know if it’s a politics thing. I don’t know if it’s a Coach Prime or Colorado thing. I know for sure if I was at another institution, this would’ve been a lot easier.”

That is a serious allegation, although there is currently no established evidence that the NCAA has treated Christensen differently because he plays for Sanders or Colorado.

His comments instead reflect the frustration of a player who believes the process is costing him an opportunity to prepare for a potentially important season.

Christensen questions why similar cases moved faster

The timing is particularly damaging because Christensen is missing the portion of the year when players establish themselves within a new defensive system.

He cannot simply replace weeks of fall camp by training independently in Florida. Colorado's defensive linemen are already building chemistry, learning assignments and competing for playing time, while Christensen remains separated from the team as his legal case continues.

His frustration has also been heightened by other recent eligibility cases. His attorney, Darren Heitner , has pointed toward rulings involving other athletes as evidence that players in comparable circumstances have received relief.

Recent litigation has challenged the NCAA's approach to its five-year eligibility framework, with courts issuing injunctions that have allowed some athletes to continue competing.

“We provided every similar case to the judge,” Ezra Christensen said. “These guys got their injunctions, and there’s no difference from my case. What’s taking you two weeks to decide?”

The wider legal landscape has indeed become complicated. In a separate Colorado case, a federal judge granted a preliminary injunction involving athletes seeking a fifth season, and on August 10 the court rejected the NCAA's attempt to stay that injunction while its appeal proceeds.

Christensen's own case, however, remains distinct and still requires a ruling.

The consequences extend beyond football. Christensen's background makes the uncertainty particularly significant.

He grew up in an orphanage in Sierra Leone, was adopted at 16 and arrived in American football without the knowledge of NCAA eligibility rules.

His high school career was also disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, before he eventually worked his way through junior college and into the FBS. His attorney has argued that those unusual circumstances should be considered in determining his eligibility.

That journey makes the current impasse especially painful. Christensen had already established himself as a productive college defender and was viewed as a potential NFL prospect before arriving in Boulder.

PFF previously ranked him among the top defensive tackles in the country, while his 40 pressures and six sacks at New Mexico State demonstrated the disruptive ability Colorado hoped to add to its defensive front.

For Sanders and Colorado, his availability could significantly strengthen the defense. For Christensen , though, the immediate concern is much more personal: every day spent waiting is another day of preparation he cannot recover.

The suggestion of a “Coach Prime tax” remains Christensen's suspicion rather than a proven explanation for the delay.

The NCAA's eligibility dispute is part of a much broader battle over how college football should handle athletes whose careers have been shaped by junior college, transfers and changing eligibility regulations.

Until the court makes its decision, Christensen can only train away from Boulder and wait.

His original ambitions for the season may have included a major statistical campaign and a run toward the NFL. For now, simply getting onto the field for Colorado has become the priority.

articles.title: Nebraska designer suing Deion Sanders for failing to make payment after creating logos for P21ME and TRUTH
articles.standfirst: A designer claims his work helped build Sanders’ brand but promised opportunities never came
articles.summary: A designer claims his work helped build Sanders’ brand but promised opportunities never came
articles.body:
Deion Sanders ’ “Prime” brand has become one of the most recognizable identities in sports, appearing across merchandise, partnerships and Colorado football .

Now, the origins of some of that branding are at the center of a federal lawsuit accusing Sanders of using a designer’s work without properly compensating him.

Nebraska designer Alan Tipp filed a lawsuit against Sanders and his business agency, SMAC Entertainment, in January 2025, alleging that he created the P21ME and TRUTH logos for Sanders in 2011 but was never paid for their continued use.

Sanders and SMAC Entertainment have denied the allegations through their attorneys, and the case remains active in federal court. Tipp ’s complaint claims he developed the logos after Sanders contacted him after seeing his previous design work.

The designs featured elements connected to Sanders ’ identity, including his former No.21 jersey number and his “Prime Time” nickname.

The lawsuit alleges those logos later became part of Sanders’ wider commercial brand, appearing on products and partnerships involving companies such as Nike, Under Armour, Blenders and Colorado merchandise after Sanders became the Buffaloes ’ head coach in 2022.

“Tipp has never been compensated, in any way, for his services by any of the Defendants or for Defendants’ use of the Works,” the complaint states.

“As a result of the direct and indirect use of the Works, the Defendants have received and continue to receive a substantial amount of revenue.”

Tipp is seeking more than $75,000 in damages and is asking the court to void the agreement that transferred rights to the designs.

Dispute over promises made to designer

The central argument in Tipp ’s lawsuit revolves around a 2011 agreement that he claims he signed after discussions with Sanders and SMAC Entertainment executive Sam Morini .

According to the complaint, Tipp was told he would become part of Sanders ’ marketing team and would have opportunities to work on projects including Sanders ’ sunglasses line and merchandise collaborations with Nike.

However, Tipp claims those opportunities never materialized after he signed away his rights to the logos.

“Each of these statements were false at the time they were made and Morini, SMAC, and Sanders knew them to be false statements of fact,” the lawsuit states.

The complaint alleges Sanders and his representatives “began evading Tipp” shortly after the agreement was completed.

Sanders has disputed that version of events, arguing the logos were already connected to his brand before Tipp ’s claims.

In a court declaration, Sanders stated the designs were tied to an Under Armour endorsement deal from 2011 and said no one challenged his use of the logos until the lawsuit was filed.

The coach and SMAC Entertainment have asked the court to issue a summary judgment rather than allowing the case to proceed to trial.

The lawsuit arrives during another busy legal period for Sanders , who is preparing for his fourth season leading Colorado. He's also involved in a separate dispute connected to his son Shilo Sanders ’ bankruptcy proceedings and whether he must provide testimony.

As the federal case continues, the dispute will determine whether Tipp has a valid claim to ownership and compensation connected to a brand that has grown into a major part of Sanders ’ public image.

articles.title: Marshall Manning goes viral in high school debut with a play that shows why everyone is watching
articles.summary: Marshall Manning already carries one of the most famous last names in football, but his first viral moment at Baylor School gave fans something beyond his family history to talk about.
articles.body:
Marshall Manning already carries one of the most famous last names in football, but his first viral moment at Baylor School gave fans something beyond his family history to talk about.

The 2030 quarterback and son of Peyton Manning showed impressive mobility on the play, escaping pressure and keeping the action alive before delivering the ball with poise. For a young quarterback making his debut, there was no panic in the sequence just movement, awareness and control.

Naturally, being a Manning means almost everything he does will be watched closely. But this particular clip has taken that attention to another level, surpassing 21 million views since it was posted on August 20 and generating enormous interest around what could come next.

The last name creates expectations, but the play speaks for itself. Marshall still has a long way to go and plenty to prove, yet for one viral sequence, the young quarterback offered a glimpse of why so many people are already watching.

articles.title: 16-year-old girl storms football field and tackles middle school player before facing assault charge
articles.summary: A middle school football game in Middle Tennessee took an unexpected turn when a 16-year-old girl ran onto the field and went directly toward one of the players.
articles.body:
A middle school football game in Middle Tennessee took an unexpected turn when a 16-year-old girl ran onto the field and went directly toward one of the players.

The video captures the teenager coming in from outside the play before wrapping up the young player and bringing him to the ground with a forceful tackle. For a moment, the scene looks almost like part of the game except she wasn't supposed to be on the field at all.

The incident didn't end when the players left the field. The 16-year-old was later charged with assault in connection with the tackle and has reportedly been banned from attending school activities for one year.

It's the kind of clip that can look surreal when watched for only a few seconds, but the consequences were very real. What happened in the middle of a football game ultimately became a legal and disciplinary matter.

articles.title: 16-year-old girl who tackled middle school football player reveals why she stormed the field
articles.standfirst: The viral tackle has now led to criminal charges and a lifetime school district ban
articles.summary: The viral tackle has now led to criminal charges and a lifetime school district ban
articles.body:
A middle school football game in Tennessee suddenly became something much more serious when a 16-year-old girl ran out of the stands, charged onto the field and tackled one of the players.

The incident happened Tuesday night during a game between South Middle School and Cornersville Middle School at Franklin County High School in Winchester . South had just scored a touchdown and extra point when a scuffle broke out between two players. That's when Addison Hunnicutt entered the field and went directly toward the South Middle player involved.

Video shows Hunnicutt wrapping up the player and taking him to the ground. After he got back to his feet, she appeared to shove him down again before an adult intervened. Officials immediately ended the game and cleared the stadium. Authorities later confirmed that no injuries were reported .

The 16-year-old says she was protecting her younger brother

Hunnicutt has since offered an explanation for what triggered the extraordinary reaction. She said the Cornersville player involved in the confrontation was her younger brother and claimed she had watched another player grab his facemask and swing him around. Her attorney has similarly characterized her actions as an attempt to protect her brother .

Whatever her motivation, the consequences were immediate. School resource officers met Hunnicutt as she left the field, and she was eventually released to her parents. The Franklin County Sheriff's Office charged the teenager with assault and disorderly conduct .

The punishment didn't stop there. Franklin County Schools issued Hunnicutt a lifetime trespass ban from all district properties, while the Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association banned her from attending Cornersville Middle School home and away athletic events for one year.

articles.title: Marshall Manning goes viral in high school debut as Peyton Manning’s son shows what all the hype is about
articles.standfirst: One play was enough to put another Manning quarterback in the spotlight
articles.summary: One play was enough to put another Manning quarterback in the spotlight
articles.body:
M arshall Manning, the son of Peyton Manning, made his high school debut for Baylor School in Tennessee and quickly gave people another reason to pay attention.

On one play, the young quarterback showed impressive mobility as he escaped pressure, kept his eyes downfield and extended the play before delivering the football.

There was nothing spectacularly complicated about it. What stood out was how comfortable he looked. Instead of panicking when the original play began to break down, Manning moved naturally, created time and remained composed, qualities that inevitably generated comparisons and excitement considering the quarterbacks in his family.

Marshall Manning is already dealing with the weight of his last name

The reaction has been enormous. A video of the play posted on August 20 surpassed 21 million views, remarkable attention for a young high school quarterback who is part of the Class of 2030 and is only beginning his career.

Of course, Marshall is Peyton Manning's son, Archie Manning's grandson and the nephew of Eli Manning. His father and uncle combined for four Super Bowl victories, while Archie spent more than a decade in the NFL.

His cousin Arch Manning is now carrying his own enormous expectations at Texas. Marshall was always going to be watched differently from most teenagers who step onto a football field.

But that's also what made his first viral moment interesting. The Manning name brought the cameras and the curiosity, but it didn't make the play for him.

Marshall still has years of development ahead and it is far too early to know where football will eventually take him. For now, though, one sequence was enough to show that the next Manning quarterback has officially entered the conversation.

articles.title: Arch Manning drops beautiful deep ball that shows why NFL scouts are so high on Texas QB
articles.standfirst: One throw offered a glimpse of the arm talent that could eventually take Manning to the NFL
articles.summary: One throw offered a glimpse of the arm talent that could eventually take Manning to the NFL
articles.body:
A rch Manning has spent most of his football life surrounded by enormous expectations. Sometimes, though, it only takes one throw to understand where some of that excitement comes from.

The Texas quarterback dropped a beautiful deep ball into his receiver's hands, combining arm strength with the touch needed to put the football exactly where it had to be . Manning gave his receiver a chance to keep running rather than forcing him to slow down or make a major adjustment, making a difficult throw look remarkably comfortable.

Arch Manning's deep ball is becoming one of his most intriguing weapons

That particular ability has caught the attention of NFL evaluators . One NFL scout reportedly described Manning's deep ball as “one of his best” traits as a prospect, an interesting assessment for a quarterback whose physical tools have been discussed since before he became Texas' full-time starter.

Manning certainly has the pedigree. He is the grandson of former NFL quarterback Archie Manning and the nephew of Super Bowl champions Peyton and Eli Manning.

But the family name can only carry a quarterback so far . Every throw, decision and performance will ultimately be judged on what Arch himself puts on tape.

And there is still plenty for him to prove. Manning has the arm talent, athleticism and size that NFL teams look for, but his development at Texas will determine just how high his professional ceiling really is.

The NFL conversation surrounding him isn't going away, especially when he produces throws like this.

articles.title: What is the first College Football game of the 2026 Season? Date, time and where to watch it
articles.standfirst: College football returns with an international Week 0 opener before the full slate arrives in September
articles.summary: College football returns with an international Week 0 opener before the full slate arrives in September
articles.body:

The FCS and FBS schedules begin at different times, while the traditional full opening weekend does not arrive until September.

articles.standfirst: The 2026 college football season is almost here, and fans can already find tickets for some of the biggest Week 1 matchups
articles.summary: The 2026 college football season is almost here, and fans can already find tickets for some of the biggest Week 1 matchups
articles.body:
C ollege football fans are preparing for the return of the 2026 season, with Week 1 bringing a packed schedule of games across the country.

For supporters hoping to experience the action inside the stadium rather than watching from home, tickets are already available for many matchups, although prices and inventory can vary considerably depending on the teams involved.

The 2026 FBS season officially gets underway during Week 0 on August 29, before the first full Saturday of college football arrives on September 5. FOX Sports lists Week 1 as running from September 3 through September 7, giving fans several days of games to choose from.

That means supporters looking to attend a game should start checking availability now, particularly for high-demand contests involving nationally recognized programs.

Fans can browse college football tickets through SeatGeek's NCAA football ticket marketplace and StubHub's NCAA football marketplace. Both platforms allow buyers to search by team, matchup and date, although prices can move as demand changes.

The most important thing for buyers to understand is that there is no single price for a Week 1 ticket. A seat in the upper level for a lower-profile matchup can cost relatively little, while a premium seat for a major rivalry or ranked showdown can be substantially more expensive.

Current listings illustrate that spread. CBS Sports' 2026 schedule showed tickets beginning at around $20 for San Jose State at USC, while NC State at Virginia had listings starting around $38 and Jacksonville State at North Dakota State around $72.

Which Week 1 games are likely to attract the biggest crowds?

Several games stand out on the opening-weekend schedule.

One of the headline contests is Clemson vs. LSU , scheduled for September 5 at 7:30 p.m. ET. Clemson's home schedule indicates that tickets are available, although inventory is limited.

Another major attraction is Boise State at Oregon, which is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on September 5. There is also Wisconsin vs. Notre Dame , which will take place at Lambeau Field in Green Bay on September 6 at 7:30 p.m. ET.

For fans seeking a less expensive way into college football, there are plenty of alternatives. CBS Sports' listings currently show some Week 0 and opening-week games with starting prices well below those associated with the marquee contests.

Hawaii at Stanford, for example, was listed from roughly $14, while New Mexico State at Florida State started around $36.

The first FBS game of the season is actually North Carolina vs. TCU in Dublin, Ireland, on August 29. The Aer Lingus College Football Classic kicks off at noon ET at Aviva Stadium and will be broadcast on ESPN.

How to save money on Week 1 tickets

The simplest way to keep costs down is to compare multiple listings before buying. Prices on resale marketplaces can fluctuate based on demand, remaining inventory and proximity to kickoff.

Buyers should also look beyond the headline games. If the primary goal is simply to attend a college football game, choosing a less-hyped matchup can dramatically reduce the cost of admission.

It is also worth checking the school's official ticket office before purchasing from a resale marketplace. Some programs may still have standard tickets available, potentially avoiding the additional costs associated with secondary-market purchases.

At the same time, fans should pay close attention to the final price at checkout rather than focusing exclusively on the initial listing price. Service fees and other charges can increase the amount ultimately paid.

Week 1 ticket availability is also likely to change rapidly. Some games already have limited inventory, while others offer a much wider selection.

USA TODAY's recent ticket guides for programs including Clemson and Texas Tech similarly note that tickets for the 2026 season are available, with limited inventory for certain games.

For fans determined to be in the stadium when the 2026 college football campaign gets serious, the best strategy is therefore to identify the matchup first, compare the official market with resale platforms, and then check the complete price before committing.

With the season opener only days away and the first full Saturday arriving September 5, waiting too long could mean fewer seating choices, particularly for the biggest games.

articles.title: Deion Sanders makes false claim about the Shilo case that led to his bankruptcy: “He's already won”
articles.standfirst: An $11.89 million judgment remains at the center of the case
articles.summary: An $11.89 million judgment remains at the center of the case
articles.body:
With Colorado days away from opening its season, Deion Sanders is trying to wave away the legal drama surrounding son Shilo Sanders . His description of the case, however, doesn't line up neatly with what the court record shows.

Asked Monday about a subpoena requiring him to testify in Shilo ’s upcoming bankruptcy trial, Sanders insisted his son had already prevailed once before.

“You know Shilo won this case previously, right?” Sanders said. “Anybody know that? Raise your hand if you know that, if you knew that, that Shilo got awarded money for this.”

He added: “I can’t wait till it’s over and he gets to tell his story. He already won this case, you know?”

The problem is that the central dispute now before the bankruptcy court stems from an $11.89 million judgment entered against Shilo Sanders , not a case he previously won.

What Shilo actually faces in bankruptcy court

The underlying lawsuit was filed by former school security guard John Darjean , who accused Shilo of assaulting him in 2015 while trying to confiscate his phone.

That case eventually produced an $11.89 million default judgment in 2022 after Shilo failed to appear for trial. He later filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in 2023 after Darjean sought to collect on the judgment.

The upcoming trial isn't about whether that judgment exists. The question is whether Shilo can discharge the debt through bankruptcy.

Darjean argues that the debt should survive because it allegedly arose from a “willful and malicious injury,” an exception under bankruptcy law. Shilo ’s attorneys maintain that he acted in self-defense and should be allowed to discharge the obligation.

The earlier “win” referenced by Deion Sanders appears to involve separate claims Shilo brought against Focus Learning Academy and founder Leroy McClure , which were resolved through a confidential settlement in 2019.

The judge in that matter made clear the settlement did “not affect any other pending claims, including but not limited to those claims by Plaintiff John Darjean.”

Deion says subpoena is no distraction

The legal timing is awkward for Colorado. The bankruptcy trial is scheduled to begin August 31 and could run through September 4. The Buffaloes are due to travel September 1 ahead of their opener at Georgia Tech on September 3.

Darjean ’s attorney subpoenaed Deion Sanders to testify, while Sanders ’ attorney, Harvey Steinberg , has asked Judge Michael Romero to quash it.

Asked whether that represented a distraction, Sanders dismissed the idea. “Dude, you think that's my first subpoena?” he said. “When you have it, when you him, when you that, you get sued.”

He added: “I don't know anyone that's a game changer, a way maker, that is not dealing with some type of lawsuit.”

What happens next will determine whether Shilo Sanders can escape the eight-figure judgment through bankruptcy. Until then, Deion Sanders ’ assertion that his son already “won” oversimplifies a legal fight that remains unresolved.

articles.body:
College football returns in force this week, but following every game will require almost as much planning as picking which ones to watch.

The first full slate of the 2026 season stretches from Thursday through Monday , with games appearing across ESPN, ABC, FOX, NBC, CBS, FS1, Big Ten Network, ACC Network, SEC Network, ESPNU and CBS Sports Network.

ESPN+, Peacock, HBO Max and several conference streaming platforms add another option for viewers chasing games outside the national television windows.

Thursday’s schedule is headlined by Colorado visiting Georgia Tech at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN. The weekend then builds toward a Saturday loaded with recognizable programs, including Alabama, Texas, Oregon, Michigan, Georgia, Ohio State and LSU .

One of the biggest prime-time games sends Clemson to LSU at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC, while Boise State visits Oregon at 3:30 p.m. on CBS.

Biggest College Football Week 1 games to watch

ABC carries three major Saturday windows, beginning with East Carolina at Alabama at noon. Auburn and Baylor meet at Mercedes-Benz Stadium at 3:30 p.m., before Clemson-LSU takes over prime time.

ESPN has Texas State-Texas at 3:30 p.m. and Missouri State-Texas A&M at 7 p.m., while FOX carries North Texas-Indiana and Boston College-Cincinnati .

NBC gets Western Michigan-Michigan on Saturday night before returning Sunday with two significant games. Washington State-Washington at 4 p.m. and Notre Dame-Wisconsin from Lambeau Field at 7:30 p.m.

Sunday also features Ole Miss-Louisville on ABC, before SMU and Florida State close the extended Week 1 schedule Monday night on ESPN.

Which streaming services carry College Football Week 1?

ESPN+ has the largest number of streaming-only games, making it particularly important for viewers following programs outside the marquee national broadcasts.

Peacock carries Eastern Illinois-Minnesota , while HBO Max is listed alongside TNT for Coastal Carolina-West Virginia . SEC Network+ and other conference digital services handle additional games.

DIRECTV MySports is another option for combining many of the major sports networks in one package, although channel availability can vary by market and some streaming-only games may still require the appropriate service.

articles.title: Paul Finebaum destroys Bill Belichick's character and makes bold prediction about his future: "He's a bully"
articles.standfirst: The famous college football analyst has lit into the much-maligned North Carolina head coach ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.summary: The famous college football analyst has lit into the much-maligned North Carolina head coach ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Heading into the 2026 college football season, most eyes are on the usual suspects: Texas , Ohio State , Notre Dame , and some other big schools. But many also have an eye on the North Carolina Tar Heels , for obvious reasons.

Bill Belichick 's first year in college football, in 2025, was an abject disaster. UNC looked ill-prepared for most games , and the program made headlines more because of Belichick's girlfriend, Jordon Hudson , than their performance on the field.

Before the 2026 season has even kicked off, UNC has been in the spotlight for the wrong reasons yet again . The university placed the football program's general manager Michael Lombardi, Belichick's good friend, on leave . He's still not working with the program with the season set to get underway soon.

Paul Finebaum says Bill Belichick will be fired before the end of 2026 UNC season

All of the warning signs have notable college football analyst Paul Finebaum expecting the worst in 2026. In fact, he believes Belichick won't make it to the end of the year at North Carolina . While explaining why, Finebaum also lit into Belichick's personality and character .

I'm not pulling for Bill Belichick. He's a grouch. He's a bully. And his career in college is about to go down in flames. He lost Michael Lombardi, his chief assistant and GM. His son disappeared from the staff a couple of weeks ago as defensive coordinator. It is mass chaos in Chapel Hill... I don't think Bill Belichick is going to survive until the end of the season.

Clearly, Belichick doesn't have a lot of fans right now, especially in the college football landscape. The only way to win any of them back is to start winning football games with the Tar Heels.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin's shady tactics spark major change in college football: Rival conference responds with new rule
articles.standfirst: The newly hired LSU head coach has rubbed people the wrong way with his latest move.
articles.summary: The newly hired LSU head coach has rubbed people the wrong way with his latest move.
articles.body:
Since the establishment of NIL and the transfer portal , college football players have gotten a massive advantage over previous generations. There's no denying that student-athletes now have more earning power and flexibility than ever before.

But the landscape of college football changing so dramatically has not been well-received by everyone. In fact, many fans believe the sport is much worse off now due to constantly changing rosters and an even greater disparity among big, medium and small programs . This week, that notion has only been amplified, thanks to Lane Kiffin .

Lane Kiffin to poach Cleveland Browns player Dae'Quan Wright

LSU 's newest head coach is close to pulling off an unfathomable and unprecedented move. He will somehow poach tight end Dae'Quan Wright and convince him to join LSU. Wright was already on an NFL roster , having signed with the Cleveland Browns after being waived by the Philadelphia Eagles during his undrafted free agent contract this offseason.

Obviously, the flood gates have now been opened by Kiffin . Wright would normally not even have college eligibility left, but the NCAA implemented a new five-year eligibility rule that Wright is planning to take advantage of - especially since he wasn't going to make the Browns' 53-man roster.

Big Ten refuses to let NFL players come back to college football in their conference

Now privy to Kiffin's tactics and hoping to keep college football from becoming the Wild Wild West, the Big Ten conference has put their foot down with a new rule: No NFL player can join a team in their conference .

This won't be the last time we hear of this topic, but a major conference like the Big Ten making that decision, unanimously, speaks volumes.

articles.title: An ESPN analyst isn't very optimistic about Deion Sanders' new season with the Colorado Buffaloes
articles.standfirst: Rece Davis believes reaching a bowl game would be a major achievement for Colorado in 2026
articles.summary: Rece Davis believes reaching a bowl game would be a major achievement for Colorado in 2026
articles.body:
D eion Sanders ' fourth season at Colorado is approaching with plenty of questions surrounding the Buffaloes , and ESPN analyst Rece Davis is not expecting the program to make a dramatic return to prominence.

Colorado's trajectory under Sanders has been difficult to predict. The Buffaloes went 1-11 before his arrival, improved to 4-8 during his first season in 2023 and then produced a 9-4 record in 2024. That breakthrough campaign put Colorado firmly back in the national conversation.

The momentum disappeared in 2025, however, when the Buffaloes dropped to 3-9 and struggled badly in Big 12 play, finishing 1-8 in conference games. Davis now believes another difficult campaign could be ahead.

“I don’t expect them to go to a bowl game this year,” Rece Davis said on his August 25 ESPN podcast.

“I don’t think that this has been some type of massive failure as an experiment or as a chance at Deion Sanders kind of using his celebrity to build awareness and build attraction to his program. …He’s invested in trying to impact his players the best way he possibly can, both on and off the field.”

That distinction is important. Davis is not arguing that Sanders ' tenure has been a failure. Instead, he believes Colorado has yet to demonstrate that the program can consistently compete without the extraordinary talent that helped fuel its 2024 resurgence.

Colorado must prove it can win without Hunter and Shedeur

The biggest challenge facing Sanders is replacing the production and influence of Travis Hunter and Shedeur Sanders .

Hunter became one of the most versatile players in college football during his Colorado career, starring as both a wide receiver and cornerback before becoming the No. 1 overall selection in the 2025 NFL Draft.

Shedeur Sanders , meanwhile, was the centerpiece of the Buffaloes' offense and was selected by the Cleveland Browns in the fifth round of the same draft.

Their departures left Colorado without two players who were responsible for a huge portion of the team's identity.

“I mean, they had one really good year with Shedeur and T ravis Hunter ,” Davis said. “But at some point, you’ve got to continue the production. And I think they’ll be competitive. I’ll be surprised if they get to a bowl game this year. I think that would constitute a really, really good season for them.”

There are reasons for Colorado supporters to remain hopeful. Sanders has worked to rebuild the roster through the transfer portal, bringing in players such as former Texas wide receiver DeAndre Moore Jr. , former Tennessee safety Boo Carter and Danny Scudero , who led the FBS in receiving yards in 2025.

Scudero's health is an important storyline after he dealt with an injury during preseason camp.

Sanders has also reshaped his coaching staff. Brennan Marion took over as offensive coordinator in December, giving Colorado another new voice as it attempts to develop an offense capable of functioning without Shedeur.

The problem is that collecting talent and turning it into a cohesive team are two very different challenges.

Colorado's schedule provides little margin for error. The Buffaloes open the season on September 3 against Georgia Tech before facing Weber State and then entering Big 12 competition.

The conference schedule includes difficult assignments against teams such as Arizona State, Texas Tech and Houston.

The opener against Georgia Tech could be particularly revealing. The Yellow Jackets defeated Colorado 27-20 in Boulder last season, giving the Buffaloes an immediate opportunity to demonstrate that the program has moved forward.

Ultimately, Davis ' prediction places considerable pressure on Sanders. A bowl appearance would require Colorado to reach at least six wins, and the ESPN analyst believes getting there would represent a genuinely strong season.

For Sanders, the task is therefore bigger than simply replacing two stars. He must show that the culture and structure he built in Boulder can produce sustained success even after the most recognizable players from his early Colorado era have moved on.

articles.title: The Cavinder Twins show off one of the most special dinners of their lives
articles.standfirst: The former basketball players celebrated the launch of Go-Two with a stylish night filled with personalized details and a meaning that goes far beyond a celebration.
articles.summary: The former basketball players celebrated the launch of Go-Two with a stylish night filled with personalized details and a meaning that goes far beyond a celebration.
articles.body:
Haley and Hanna Cavinder shared the same goal since they were little: to one day create a business together . That dream finally took shape with Go-Two, their new brand, which they decided to celebrate with a special dinner alongside their friends and an atmosphere designed for the occasion.

Two looks for a dreamy night

For the dinner, Haley and Hanna chose two-piece sets that showcased different styles. One wore an all-black look with texture and floral details, while the other opted for a brown outfit with an asymmetrical neckline and a white detail .

What was at the center of the celebration?

The cake was one of the most eye-catching details of the night. The twins chose a white, heart-shaped cake decorated with small colorful gems, with the name “GO-TWO” placed in the center.

The table also featured personalized glasses and other details related to their brand.

However, what they were celebrating went far beyond a night among friends.

What is Go-Two and why is it so important to the Cavinder Twins?

Go-Two is a new wellness and supplement brand focused on an active lifestyle. The launch began with two powdered products: Debloat, designed as a supplement to reduce stomach bloating, and Sleep Support, aimed at rest and relaxation.

The arrival of the brand represents a new chapter for Haley and Hanna , who built a huge public presence through basketball, social media and the commercial deals that shaped the early NIL era.

The twins were among the athletes who made the most of that transformation in college sports. Their reach on social media, especially on TikTok, allowed them to build a community that later translated into partnerships with companies such as Under Armour and Victoria's Secret PINK, as well as various collaborations in the fashion and entertainment industries.

articles.title: SEC and Big Ten block pro players returning to NCAA: Football and Basketball impacted
articles.standfirst: The Southeastern Conference has joined the Big Ten in cracking down on an emerging trend.
articles.summary: The Southeastern Conference has joined the Big Ten in cracking down on an emerging trend.
articles.body:
The Southeastern Conference passed a rule Tuesday banning players who have been drafted by NFL , NBA or WNBA teams or listed on rosters in those leagues, joining the Big Ten in taking a strong stand against an unexpected surge of pro players trying to return to college with the NCAA mired in a sprawling legal fight over eligibility.

The SEC 's rule goes beyond the one adopted earlier in the day by the Big Ten, which only included football in its decision and is expected address other sports later.

The news was the latest in a head-spinning week of court rulings, emergency rulemaking sessions and player signings, all of which point to a college sports landscape in disarray. The moves by the nation's two biggest conferences, four days before the start of football season, are intended to tamp down the latest crisis — one involving players who came back to college after being released from pro rosters.

“I feel like I took a freaking gummy,” said Sean McVay , the coach of the Los Angeles Rams, when asked about the prospect of a player he released returning to college. “I don’t even understand it.”

The rules — which seem likely to be challenged in court — came after a series of losses for the NCAA in state courts around the country, where judges are granting players who graduated high school in 2022 a fifth year of eligibility. In June, the NCAA passed a rule giving most players five years to finish five seasons of eligibility in college, but did not grandfather in the Class of ’22 .

Hundreds of those players saw their fourth — and supposedly final — year of eligibility run out last spring. They are arguing that they’re being denied educational opportunities and the chance to earn name, image and likeness money that they could get in a fifth year.

College rosters are largely set and incoming freshmen and other new players on teams are now faced with sudden competition from athletes whose eligibility had supposedly run out.

LSU was quick to nab players after court rulings

The SEC rule puts LSU on notice. This week, Tigers coach Lane Kiffin was adding Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris , a pair of undrafted players out of Mississippi who had tryouts in the NFL over the summer, but were released by their teams during training camp.

The rule, which also applies to players signed by the NBA G League, will impact players like R.J. Luis Jr. . On Monday , the former St. John's star won a court ruling that allowed him to sign with Will Wade ’s basketball program at LSU despite having briefly been under contract with the Jazz and Celtics of the NBA.

Kiffin suggested in a news conference Monday that if LSU didn’t take these newly eligible players, other teams certainly would. Now, nobody can — at least not among the 34 teams that make up the two biggest leagues in college and play an outsize role in spearheading policy across the industry.

There was no immediate comment from LSU.

“Over 100 athletes in multiple sports were cleared and said you could go play. That’s a court order,” Kiffin said earlier Tuesday on “The Pat McAfee Show” on ESPN . “If you think back on all the different court orders of great players that were granted -- whether that’s Diego Pavia or, now, Trinidad (Chambliss) that were allowed to play a sixth year, we followed all court orders. I think you get into a really interesting situation as a conference if you’re now saying, ‘Well, we’re not going to follow this court order.’"

The Big Ten's penalties for violating its rule include a half-season suspension for the head coach and a fine for the school. The SEC did not immediately divulge its penalties, though commissioner Greg Sankey is expected to have wide latitude in figuring out punishment.

The other Power Four leagues, the Atlantic Coast and Big 12 conferences, are expected to discuss the issue Wednesday .

“I don’t think anybody in our league likes the idea of taking away opportunities from existing college students and graduating high school players, which is exactly what is happening when a school signs a player out of an NFL camp to their team,” Wake Forest athletic director John Currie wrote in a text message to The Associated Press.

The leagues and NCAA are using the eligibility crisis as a selling point for the Protect College Sports Act , a bill in the Senate that would give the NCAA some protection against the sort of lawsuits that are upending college athletics.

But that bill is weeks away from a vote. Football season starts Saturday, with the featured game taking place in Ireland, where TCU faces North Carolina .

“It’s a rudderless ship right now,” TCU coach Sonny Dykes said. “I mean, I don’t know who’s in charge of football anymore.”

Duke coach Manny Diaz said the Power Four conferences need to present a unified front.

“You wouldn’t run any other type of corporation, organization, anything else, the way we’re being run right now,” he said. “And so I hope the leagues do step up because somebody has to right now, because when there’s a vacuum, this is what you see.”

articles.standfirst: Recent clock changes have reduced snaps, but the viewing experience remains much longer than allotted 60 minutes
articles.summary: Recent clock changes have reduced snaps, but the viewing experience remains much longer than allotted 60 minutes
articles.body:
College football has tried to speed itself up. The surprising part is that fans may not have noticed much difference.

Rule changes introduced over the past several seasons have cut the number of plays in a typical game, particularly after the NCAA stopped the clock from automatically pausing after every first down outside the final two minutes of each half.

Yet the average game still stretches far beyond its 60 minutes of official playing time.

In 2024, the average college football game lasted 3 hours, 27 minutes , tied for the second-longest mark since the NCAA began tracking game duration in 2008.

The College Football Playoff was even slower, with its 11 games averaging roughly 3 hours, 29.5 minutes .

That happened even though total combined plays fell to about 175 per game, around five fewer than the level seen before the first-down rule was changed.

Fewer plays haven't meant shorter games

The first-down clock rule was one of the most significant timing changes college football had made in decades. Since 1968, the clock had traditionally stopped after first downs.

Beginning in 2023, it was allowed to continue running outside the final two minutes of each half, bringing the college game closer to the NFL model.

The motivation was not simply about creating shorter broadcasts. Player safety was an important part of the discussion because fewer snaps theoretically mean fewer opportunities for injuries.

“Commissioners have begun to look at plays per game rather than duration,” an NCAA source said, as per CBS.

That distinction matters because the rule appears to be doing what it was designed to do. The number of plays has fallen. The length of the broadcast has not followed at the same pace.

Television breaks remain one of the biggest reasons. Networks generally build multiple commercial windows into each quarter, and those stoppages can add dozens of minutes to the viewing experience.

“It has more to do with how much time it takes coming in and out of breaks,” a television industry source told CBS. “It’s not a material difference.”

Another industry source was even more direct: “Nobody likes to say this but you know it, it’s the media timeouts.”

Games can push towards four hours

Commercials are only part of the equation. College halftime typically lasts 20 minutes, while replay reviews, penalties, injuries, scoring plays and timeouts can all add substantial real-world time.

Overtime can stretch things even further. The 2024 Peach Bowl between Texas and Arizona State lasted more than four hours after going beyond regulation.

The official game is 60 minutes, divided into four 15-minute quarters. The actual event is usually much longer.

A normal televised matchup will often last somewhere between about 3 hours, 15 minutes and 3 hours, 30 minutes. Games involving overtime, lengthy replay reviews or heavy commercial loads can easily push closer to four hours.

The irony is that the sport has successfully reduced snaps while still asking fans to dedicate most of an afternoon or evening to one game.

articles.title: Arch Manning draws criticism after offseason foot surgery and a “Little Chubby” comment
articles.standfirst: Manning and the Longhorns will open the season at home against Texas State on September 5
articles.summary: Manning and the Longhorns will open the season at home against Texas State on September 5
articles.body:
College football is officially back this weekend with Week 0 featuring eight games on Saturday, though the broader slate expands next week when powerhouses take the field, including reigning champions Indiana, early favorites Ohio State , and the Texas Longhorns anchored by Arch Manning , widely projected as the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft .

Texas enters the preseason ranked fifth in the AP poll, and while Manning stands among the premier Heisman Trophy favorites , navigating the schedule will be a grueling test. Out of their 12 regular-season games, the Longhorns will square off against seven opponents currently ranked inside the AP Top 25 .

Following their opening matchup against Texas State , the schedule features a marquee home showdown against Ohio State , a hostile road trip to Tennessee , the annual Red River Rivalry clash against Oklahoma in Dallas, home dates with Florida and Ole Miss , and brutal late-season away battles versus LSU and Texas A&M .

Arch Manning Addresses Weight Fluctuations

With soaring expectations in Austin as the program chases its first national title since 2005 , every word and movement from the Texas quarterback instantly sparks a national media frenzy, making his recent candid remarks about his physical transformation a major talking point.

Back at the Manning Passing Academy in late June, Manning weighed approximately 235 pounds after bulking up during his spring rehabilitation. However, he trimmed down over the summer to regain his trademark mobility ahead of the fall, currently operating at around 220 pounds .

"I was a little chubby," Manning admitted candidly this week. That weight fluctuation stemmed back to January when he underwent a minor foot surgery , a post-procedure recovery that temporarily restricted his movement and limited his conditioning routine.

While such shifts are completely standard for injured athletes, Manning explained that he initially wanted to test how carrying extra mass would feel on the gridiron, though he ultimately realized the added bulk made his rushing mobility much more difficult.

Despite minor offseason hurdles, Manning's stellar production across his first full campaign as the undisputed starter speaks volumes: he racked up 3,163 passing yards, 36 total touchdowns (including 10 rushing scores), a 61.4% completion percentage, and just seven interceptions.

articles.title: NCAAF Predictions Week 1: These are the best College Football picks for first week of the season
articles.standfirst: The first full weekend could reshape expectations quickly, especially for teams under pressure
articles.summary: The first full weekend could reshape expectations quickly, especially for teams under pressure
articles.body:
The 2026 college football season wastes little time creating meaningful matchups.

After Week 0 gets things moving, the first full slate over Labor Day weekend brings a mix of ranked showdowns, neutral-site games and difficult road assignments.

Several teams expected to feature in the College Football Playoff race will have a chance to establish themselves immediately, while others could find their season under pressure before September has properly begun.

Here are the Week 1 winners that stand out most.

Auburn and Oregon have strong opening matchups

Baylor vs. Auburn — Pick: Auburn

The Alex Golesh era at Auburn begins with an intriguing neutral-site game in Atlanta.

Golesh brought quarterback Byrum Brown with him from South Florida, giving the Tigers familiarity at the most important position while installing a new offense.

Baylor should be more dangerous with former Florida quarterback DJ Lagway , but turnovers remain a concern.

Auburn has the stronger overall roster and should also enjoy a significant crowd advantage at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Boise State at No.2 Oregon — Pick: Oregon

Boise State has caused Oregon plenty of problems before, including a close meeting in Eugene in 2024, but this assignment looks considerably tougher.

The Ducks return quarterback Dante Moore , plenty of skill-position talent and an experienced defensive front. New coordinators introduce an early unknown, but Oregon should have enough depth and explosiveness to control the game.

LSU gets nod in Lane Kiffin’s debut

No.23 Clemson at No.13 LSU — Pick: LSU

One of the weekend’s biggest games will also be the first major look at Lane Kiffin ’s LSU.

The Tigers attacked the transfer portal heavily during the offseason and will unveil a significantly reshaped roster at Tiger Stadium.

Clemson offers more continuity, but Dabo Swinney ’s program enters after a disappointing 7-6 season and has lost three consecutive openers.

Winning in Baton Rouge would represent an enormous statement for Clemson . LSU is the safer pick.

Louisville vs. No.10 Ole Miss — Pick: Ole Miss

Louisville has enough offensive talent to make this uncomfortable, particularly after adding former Ohio State quarterback Lincoln Kienholz .

Ole Miss , however, enters with the higher ceiling.

Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy give the Rebels an experienced offensive foundation, and their overall talent edge should eventually tell.

Notre Dame and SMU can make early statements

Wisconsin vs. No.5 Notre Dame — Pick: Notre Dame

Lambeau Field provides one of Week 1’s best settings, but Notre Dame looks like the significantly stronger team.

Wisconsin remains in rebuilding mode under Luke Fickell , while the Fighting Irish enter the season with genuine national championship expectations.

Notre Dame should be able to control the line of scrimmage and avoid an opening-week upset.

No. 20 SMU at Florida State — Pick: SMU

Florida State badly needs signs of progress after winning just seven games across the previous two seasons.

Unfortunately for the Seminoles , SMU brings back 11 starters and an established quarterback in Kevin Jennings . The Mustangs have also proven they can consistently win inside the ACC.

Florida State should be improved, but SMU ’s continuity makes the Mustangs the better Week 1 pick.

articles.title: Who is Charlie Becker? The Indiana wide receiver that pledged to donate $1,000 for every touchdown he scores to help fight ALS
articles.standfirst: Hoosiers receiver is turning every score into support for ALS research after his aunt’s diagnosis
articles.summary: Hoosiers receiver is turning every score into support for ALS research after his aunt’s diagnosis
articles.body:
C harlie Becker ’s breakout at Indiana gave him a bigger platform. Now he is using it for something far more personal than football .

The Indiana Hoosiers wide receiver has pledged to donate $1,000 for every touchdown he scores this season to Huddle for Hope , an ALS-focused initiative inspired by his aunt’s diagnosis.

“My family has always been super close and five years ago we learned that my aunt was diagnosed with ALS,” Becker said on The Pat McAfee Show.

“That affected all of us. I was in a spot where I really couldn't help, and I really wanted to, because there's not a cure.”

That feeling has stayed with him as his football career has grown.

Becker’s rise at Indiana gave him chance to help

Becker became a more significant part of Indiana’s offense midway through last season, scoring four touchdowns during the Hoosiers ’ run to the national championship.

With a larger role expected in 2026 and NIL money now giving him the ability to contribute financially, Becker decided to connect his production directly to the cause.

McAfee immediately added to the momentum, saying he would match Becker ’s donations.

The show also floated prominent Indiana names such as Mark Cuban , Joe Buck and former quarterback Fernando Mendoza as potential supporters.

That connection carries extra weight because Mendoza ’s mother, Elsa, has multiple sclerosis, and the former Indiana quarterback has also been active in raising awareness around neurological disease.

Huddle for Hope is expanding beyond football

Becker ’s campaign isn't limited to what happens on Saturdays. He has also partnered with Bloomington restaurant Buffalouie ’s, which created a burger tied to the fundraising effort.

Twenty percent of sales goes toward the cause, with the restaurant matching that amount.

“My aunt was diagnosed with ALS and she’s been an amazing light in my life,” Becker said in the campaign announcement. “I just want to help her as much as I can.”

Buffalouie’s owner Ed Schwartzman said he hopes the campaign can grow beyond local support.

“There could be one person who might look at this and say, you know what, I’m going to put a seven-figure check in there,” Schwartzman said.

ALS , also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease , is a progressive nervous system condition that affects the nerve cells responsible for voluntary muscle movement. There is currently no cure.

Indiana opens its 2026 season September 5 against North Texas . If Becker reaches the end zone, the scoreboard will not be the only thing that changes.

articles.title: Arch Manning has major incentive to skip 2027 NFL Draft and stay at Texas an additional year
articles.standfirst: While NFL teams waited until the 2026 NFL Draft for Manning, it turns out he could be at Texas for much longer than anticipated.
articles.summary: While NFL teams waited until the 2026 NFL Draft for Manning, it turns out he could be at Texas for much longer than anticipated.
articles.body:
Once again, expectations are extremely high for the Texas Longhorns and Arch Manning . Before the 2025 season, many penciled them in as a National Championship lock and Manning as the overwhelming Heisman Trophy favorite.

None of that played out as expected, but Manning and the Longhorns' strong finish to last season, plus a re-tooling in the offseason, has fans back on board the bandwagon. Many are yet again hoping for big things, particularly from Manning . A big season would reinforce his status as the potential No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft . That is, if he even declares.

There's still a lot that has to happen for that to come to fruition. Manning will have to play much better, much more consistently, than he did in 2025 . There also has to be a commitment from Manning to make the jump to the NFL , something that not everyone is certain of.

Todd McShay believes Arch Manning will stay two more years at Texas

Famous draft expert Todd McShay has sown doubt in regards to Manning not only being the No. 1 pick in the upcoming draft, but even entering it. McShay believes Manning could use up all of his college eligibility .

Let's back off this expectation that he's the number one overall pick and he's the guy and this is Texas' year. Because I got more news for you: I don't even know that the Mannings at this as like the swan song at Texas. There's a long history of Mannings sticking around that extra year, that people didn't think they were going to stick around, until they're right and they feel like they're ready. And I won't be surprised at all if he's in the 2028 Draft.

While many have pointed to Manning staying at Texas in order to avoid potentially joining the much-maligned Cleveland Browns franchise in the 2027 NFL Draft , Manning has a bigger incentive to stay in college.

On3 reports that Manning is making $2.5 million for the 2026 season through his NIL contract . That's in addition to his external endorsement deals. Sure, Manning would make more money in the NFL, but continuing to develop at Texas while still making a strong income could persuade him into staying longer than expected .

articles.summary: The 2026 season starts with North Carolina-TCU in Dublin before USC, Florida State and Memphis take center stage
articles.body:
College football finally takes over Saturday again, and the opening weekend of the 2026 season offers something unusual with a schedule that begins across the Atlantic and continues deep into the night in Las Vegas.

Saturday, August 29 brings the first FBS action of the new campaign, headlined by North Carolina against TCU at Aviva Stadium in Dublin. The noon ET kickoff starts a day featuring No.14 USC, Florida State, Virginia and NC State before Memphis and UNLV close the national schedule at 10 p.m. ET.

The NCAA officially describes these games as Week 0, although some schedule services list the opening weekend as Week 1. Either way, it represents the first substantial Saturday of the 2026 college football season.

ESPN, NBC, FOX, The CW and CBS Sports Network are among the national broadcasters, while ESPN+ carries much of the extensive FCS schedule.

articles.title: Who is the 11-year-old football player who has gone viral for standing an impressive 1.93 meters tall and dominating on the field?
articles.standfirst: His reported 6-foot-4 frame has made him an instant internet sensation
articles.summary: His reported 6-foot-4 frame has made him an instant internet sensation
articles.body:
An 11-year-old football player has become an unexpected social media sensation after footage of him dominating a youth game left viewers stunned by his extraordinary size.

Reportedly standing around 6-foot-4, or 1.93 meters, the youngster towers over many of the children he competes against and looks more like an older teenager than an elementary school student.

The young player reportedly competes for the Naples Bears in a 12U youth football league. A highlight video featuring him quickly spread across social media, with viewers struggling to comprehend how someone so young could be physically imposing compared with the other players on the field.

In the footage, his size immediately stands out. He’s able to power through defenders, shrug off tackles and create plays that appear almost effortless because of his considerable physical advantage.

The contrast between him and some of his opponents has also provided plenty of entertainment online, with several players appearing tiny beside him.

The unusual footage has sparked plenty of reactions from sports fans, many of whom initially questioned whether the youngster could really be 11 years old. Some social media users joked that he looked like he was old enough to have a mortgage, while others wondered how many college recruiters or NIL opportunities might already be waiting for him.

Why has the young football player gone viral?

The attention surrounding the player grew even further after Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson joined the conversation. Jackson reacted to the viral footage on Instagram, joking that the 11-year-old looked like he belonged in an 18U competition rather than playing against children in an under-12 league.

"11???? Bra 18U out there," Lamar wrote.

That reaction helped push the bizarre-looking footage to an even wider audience. However, there’s an important caveat surrounding the youngster’s reported measurements.

While reports identify him as an 11-year-old Naples Bears player, the claim that he’s exactly 6-foot-4 hasn’t been independently verified. One report also suggested that the listed height could be somewhat exaggerated.

Regardless of whether the precise measurement is accurate, there’s little doubt that the child is exceptionally large compared with his teammates and opponents. His physical presence has made his highlights particularly striking and turned an ordinary youth football game into an internet talking point.

At the same time, it’s far too early to predict where his football career will go. Children develop at different rates, and physical advantages at 11 don’t automatically translate into success at higher levels.

articles.title: Bill Belichick will be without a key figure in North Carolina when the season begins
articles.standfirst: North Carolina enters 2026 opener with key coach sidelined
articles.summary: North Carolina enters 2026 opener with key coach sidelined
articles.body:
Bill Belichick’s second season at North Carolina is set to begin with a significant absence on his coaching staff.

Defensive coordinator Steve Belichick isn’t expected to be with the Tar Heels when they open the 2026 season against TCU on Saturday, Aug. 29, in Dublin, Ireland. Steve , the son of the six-time Super Bowl champion head coach, has been on indefinite medical leave since early August.

North Carolina hasn’t provided further details about Steve’s medical situation or offered a timetable for his return. The program has also declined to provide additional public information regarding his absence.

Steve’s absence leaves the Tar Heels without the coach responsible for coordinating a defense that will be looking to make major improvements this season.

He served as North Carolina’s defensive coordinator last year after previously working on his father’s staff with the New England Patriots. He also spent the 2024 season as Washington’s defensive coordinator.

The timing is less than ideal for a team facing a challenging opening assignment against TCU on an international stage.

Bill Belichick set to take a bigger role on defense

With Steve unavailable, Bill Belichick and defensive line coach Bob Diaco have reportedly worked together throughout the preseason on defensive preparations. Bill is expected to handle the defensive play-calling duties against TCU, giving him another major responsibility on game day.

The veteran coach has previously declined to discuss his son’s medical leave in detail. Instead, he’s emphasized that North Carolina’s defense is prepared collectively by the coaching staff and that the group will continue working together despite Steve’s absence.

That approach will be tested immediately against TCU. The matchup marks North Carolina’s first international football game, with the Tar Heels traveling to Dublin for the Aer Lingus College Football Classic at Aviva Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for noon ET, with the game set to air on ESPN.

There’s plenty riding on the opener for Belichick. His first season in Chapel Hill produced a disappointing 4-8 record, and the Tar Heels are under pressure to show meaningful progress in year two.

The program will be hoping the experience of its Hall of Fame-caliber head coach can translate into better results on the field.

After facing TCU, North Carolina will return home to prepare for East Tennessee State. The Tar Heels then face a demanding stretch as they begin ACC play, making a strong opening performance even more important.

At this time the program’s attention is on getting through the season opener without Steve Belichick on the sideline. His health remains the primary concern, but his absence also places additional responsibility on his father and the rest of the defensive staff.

Bill Belichick has spent decades navigating unexpected challenges, and he’ll now face another one at North Carolina.

How effectively the Tar Heels adjust without their defensive coordinator could become one of the early storylines of the 2026 season.

articles.title: North Carolina Tar Heels vs TCU: Where to watch Bill Belichick's team's first college football game and what time it starts
articles.summary: The college football calendar kicks off in a big way. The TCU Horned Frogs open the 2026-27 NCAA Division FBS campaign by hosting the North Carolina Tar Heels in a Week 1 matchup that sportsbooks have already labeled clearly: the Fort Worth team comes in as heavy favorites, while the Tar Heels arrive as the underdog looking to pull off the surprise.
articles.body:
The college football calendar kicks off in a big way. The TCU Horned Frogs open the 2026-27 NCAA Division FBS campaign by hosting the North Carolina Tar Heels in a Week 1 matchup that sportsbooks have already labeled clearly: the Fort Worth team comes in as heavy favorites, while the Tar Heels arrive as the underdog looking to pull off the surprise.

It is the kind of clash that defines narratives from the very first weekend, with questions of discipline and form still to be written on the field.

This is a season-opening matchup, corresponding to Round 1 of the NCAA Division FBS. TCU at home carries a lot of weight in the bookmakers' reading, with Bill Belichick's North Carolina forced to travel and face an early test away from home.

In an opener like this, uncertainty is at its highest—the offensive chemistry, depth on the line, and pace of play have yet to be seen—and that always adds extra spice to the opening lines.

Game time between North Carolina vs TCU

The kickoff is scheduled for this Friday, August 27 at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time . The matchup corresponds to Round 1 of the NCAA Division FBS regular season, with the TCU Horned Frogs playing at home against the North Carolina Tar Heels.

In the rest of the United States, the game will start:

Where can you watch the game live from the United States?

Anyone who wants to watch the Tar Heels' first game, to be played at Aviva Stadium in Dublin, will be able to follow it on ESPN or via streaming on FUBO.

How do the Tar Heels and TCU arrive for the first game of the season?

Since this is the first game of the season, there is no win-loss record yet. What does speak clearly is the betting board: TCU appears with an implied 72.4% probability of winning, compared to North Carolina’s 27.6%.

It is a considerable gap for an opener, and it reflects the market’s confidence in the local favorite. Remember that in American football there is no tie on the moneyline: there are only two possible outcomes.

Betting markets: this is how things stand for the North Carolina vs TCU game

The outright winner odds leave little room for interpretation:

TCU Horned Frogs: 1.37 (implied probability 72.4%)

North Carolina Tar Heels: 3.55 (implied probability 27.6%)

At 1.37, backing TCU on the moneyline offers very little value: you're risking a lot to win a little, and in a Week 1 game—where any team can come out flat— the upset risk is not well compensated by the price .

At the other end, North Carolina at 3.55 is the classic speculative value bet: if you think the Tar Heels can steal the opener on the road, the return is attractive. The cold reading says TCU should win ; the question is whether they should win by as much as the handicap suggests.

Total points (Over/Under). The market offers two very close lines :

Over/Under 47.5: Over 1.92, Under 1.92

Over/Under 48: Over 1.94, Under 1.89

Handicap point (point spread). Here is the heart of the matchup. The available lines :

TCU -7.5 at 1.92, TCU -8 at 1.91, TCU -8.5 at 1.91, TCU -10.5 at 2.09

North Carolina +7.5 at 1.96, +8 at 1.92, +8.5 at 1.85, +10.5 at 1.71

The handicap hovers around 8 points in TCU's favor. That margin—slightly more than a touchdown and a conversion—is significant but not overwhelming.

The key is that North Carolina covers: taking +8.5 at 1.85 or even +10.5 at 1.71 protects against a close loss, a scenario that is not at all unusual when the favorite wins but doesn't pull away in its first game. Covering a double-digit spread in Week 1 is a real challenge for any home team.

articles.title: Arch Manning opens 2026 as Heisman favorite, and a new weapon could help him make family history
articles.standfirst: The senior has gradually developed into the centerpiece of Steve Sarkisian's offense
articles.summary: The senior has gradually developed into the centerpiece of Steve Sarkisian's offense
articles.body:
T he Manning family has accumulated nearly every major accomplishment a quarterback can achieve. Archie Manning became a college football legend at Ole Miss. Peyton Manning built a Hall of Fame résumé and won two Super Bowls . Eli Manning delivered two of the most memorable championship runs in NFL history.

Together, the family has produced generations of elite quarterbacks and left an indelible mark on the sport. Yet one of college football's most prestigious awards has remained surprisingly elusive. No Manning has ever won the Heisman Trophy. According to NFL.com analyst and former player Bucky Brooks, that could finally change in 2026.

Brooks recently placed Texas quarterback Arch Manning at the top of his 2026 Heisman Trophy watch list, citing the Longhorns' loaded offense and the arrival of a dynamic new playmaker who could elevate the young signal-caller's production to another level. If Brooks is right, Arch Manning may have the perfect opportunity to accomplish something neither Peyton, Eli, nor Archie ever achieved.

The Heisman favorite enters the spotlight

Expectations have followed Manning since the moment he arrived in Austin. As the nephew of Peyton and Eli Manning and the grandson of Archie Manning , he entered college football carrying one of the most recognizable surnames in sports. While the attention has often been overwhelming, Manning has gradually developed into the centerpiece of Steve Sarkisian's offense and one of the most intriguing quarterbacks in the country.

Now, with Texas once again expected to contend for a national championship, the spotlight has intensified. Brooks believes Manning is positioned to deliver the kind of statistical season that Heisman voters love. The Texas quarterback possesses the size, arm talent, mobility, and football IQ that NFL scouts covet. At 6-foot-4 and 222 pounds, he has the physical profile of a future professional starter, but it is the supporting cast around him that could ultimately separate him from the competition.

Cam Coleman could be the missing piece

One of the biggest reasons for optimism surrounding Manning's Heisman candidacy is the addition of Auburn transfer Cam Coleman. Brooks described Coleman as a potential NFL WR1 prospect, and his arrival gives Texas another explosive weapon in an offense already loaded with talent.

Coleman's ability to stretch defenses vertically could create more opportunities for Manning to attack downfield. His combination of size, speed, and ball-tracking ability makes him a dangerous target on deep routes, while his playmaking skills after the catch provide another avenue for generating big plays.

For a quarterback chasing a Heisman Trophy, explosive plays matter.

Highlight-reel touchdowns, long completions, and eye-popping statistics often shape the narrative of a Heisman campaign. Coleman appears capable of helping Manning produce all three. Brooks also noted that the receiver's versatility should allow Texas to utilize him on catch-and-run concepts, helping Manning rack up completions and maintain a high efficiency rate throughout the season.

Sarkisian's system is built for quarterback success

Talent alone does not win the Heisman Trophy. The right offensive system is equally important, and few coaches in college football are more respected for offensive design than Steve Sarkisian. Over the past several seasons, Sarkisian has consistently crafted game plans that maximize quarterback strengths and create favorable matchups for skill-position players.

His offenses are known for generating explosive plays while also manufacturing easy scoring opportunities through creative formations and route combinations. Brooks specifically pointed to Sarkisian's ability to design "winners", plays that frequently leave receivers open for uncontested touchdowns.

Those schemes not only help Texas win games , but they also boost quarterback production. If Manning is regularly throwing for touchdowns while directing one of the nation's most explosive offenses, his Heisman résumé could become difficult to ignore.
