articles.title: Wisconsin dad trips 9-year-old football player running for touchdown before police learn why he did it
articles.standfirst: What looked like an ordinary youth football run suddenly changed when an adult came off the sideline
articles.summary: What looked like an ordinary youth football run suddenly changed when an adult came off the sideline
articles.body:
A 9-year-old boy had the football in his hands and was running down the field when something happened that nobody watching a youth game should ever expect to see. An adult came onto the field, moved toward him and deliberately stuck out his leg.

The child went crashing to the ground. The person who tripped him wasn't another player, a coach or an official. Police say it was a 41-year-old father whose own child was playing for the opposing team.

The disturbing moment happened August 22 during a 10-U game between the Case Eagles and Milwaukee Colts at Case High School in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin . Video of the play shows the young Eagles player carrying the ball when the man enters the field and extends his leg into the boy's path. Somehow, the 9-year-old escaped without injury, got back up and was able to continue playing.

The father admitted to police that he was wrong

By the time Mount Pleasant police arrived , both the man and the young player had left the area. Another parent followed the man's vehicle and helped officers locate him.

Police say the father admitted that he had tripped the child and acknowledged that his actions were wrong. Bodycam footage from the encounter reportedly shows him trying to explain his reaction by expressing concern about bigger children playing against his own child.

Whatever frustration he felt, however, ended with an adult physically interfering with a 9-year-old in the middle of a football play.

Authorities considered whether the incident could qualify as physical abuse of a child under Wisconsin law, but because the boy suffered no bodily harm, police said the necessary elements for that charge were not met.

The Racine County District Attorney's Office was consulted, and the 41-year-old was ultimately cited for disorderly conduct and released.

Case Eagles coach Channing Schultz called it “the most cowardly act I've ever seen” and argued that the consequences could easily have been much worse, including a serious leg injury. The father was banned from attending games for the rest of the season, while Schultz has called for a lifetime ban.

The boy walked away physically unharmed, but the video left behind an image that is difficult to shake.

articles.title: Coach Prime opens up about the hardships of his childhood and makes a heartbreaking confession about his mother
articles.standfirst: Sanders opens up about his mother’s relentless sacrifices and the promise he made as a child
articles.summary: Sanders opens up about his mother’s relentless sacrifices and the promise he made as a child
articles.body:
Deion Sanders has spent decades building an image around confidence, success and an unmistakable larger-than-life personality.

But behind the “Coach Prime” persona is a childhood marked by financial struggles and the sacrifices of a mother who worked tirelessly to give her children a better future.

During an August 26 appearance on The Basement With Tim Ross, Sanders opened up about his upbringing in Fort Myers, Florida, and shared emotional memories of his mother, Connie Knight.

His recollections showed he grew up in a much different life from the one he enjoys today as a Pro Football Hall of Famer and college football coach.

Sanders explained that his mother worked extremely hard while raising him and his sister. Their family home eventually became condemned, and Sanders remembered growing up with rats and roaches.

One story from his childhood stood out. A Florida State donor once invited Sanders and his mother to dinner. Knight worked nights but made time to attend.

When a server asked what they wanted for their “entrée,” Sanders said he and his mother looked at each other because they didn’t know what the word meant.

“And we went, and I forget the name of the da-n restaurant. I know it was about water in Fort Myers sand; they came around, and they asked, ‘What would you be having for your entrée?’ And then my mama looked around at each other like, ‘What’s an entrée?’ We didn’t know what that was,” said Sanders .

“We haven’t been anywhere like this, where they put a napkin on your lap… So that’s where we came from, man. We didn’t know. We had rats and roaches at our old place.”

The story shows the difficult circumstances his family had endured and just how much his mother had sacrificed to provide for her children.

His mother worked at Lee Memorial Hospital and took on demanding hours to keep the household going. Sanders has spoken before about watching her work while he and his sister remained at home, an experience that left a lasting impression on him.

The promise Sanders made to his mother

Those struggles helped shape Sanders ’ ambitions from a remarkably young age. As a child, he promised himself that he'd become successful enough to make sure his mother never had to work again.

That goal became deeply connected to his pursuit of football. When the Atlanta Falcons selected Sanders with the fifth overall pick in the 1989 NFL Draft, he finally had the opportunity to turn that childhood promise into reality.

Sanders has said his mother stopped working after he entered the NFL, allowing him to provide her with the security he'd dreamed of giving her.

His success eventually allowed him to give Knight a new home in Fort Myers. The seven-bedroom, seven-bathroom property featured a swimming pool with “PRIME TIME” incorporated into its design, serving as a striking symbol of how dramatically the family’s circumstances had changed.

The original family home, meanwhile, was eventually demolished by the City of Fort Myers in 2018 after falling into severe disrepair.

Still, Sanders hasn’t forgotten what that house represented. It was where he witnessed his mother’s determination and where his ambitions first began taking shape.

articles.title: College football quarterbacks are making more money than NFL rookies through NIL deals
articles.standfirst: The top five in NIL earnings in college football are higher than the top five NFL rookies
articles.summary: The top five in NIL earnings in college football are higher than the top five NFL rookies
articles.body:
College football is back this weekend with eight games to begin the 2026 season to see who can claim the championship crown or if the Indiana Hoosiers can successfully defend their title, a feat that looks exceedingly difficult after the program lost a record 8 selections in the 2026 NFL Draft.

Out of that historic draft class, the most notable name was the first overall pick , Heisman-winning quarterback Fernando Mendoza , who stands as one of only two signal-callers taken within the first 60 picks (alongside Ty Simpson at No. 13). Mendoza enters his professional career commanding the highest salary among all rookies after signing a 4-year, $57,270,598 contract with the Las Vegas Raiders .

College QBs Out-Earn NFL Draft Picks

Ever since the Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) framework was introduced in 2021, it has completely revolutionized how young collegiate stars evaluate their timelines, making it far more lucrative for elite quarterbacks to remain on campus rather than rushing blindly into the professional ranks.

This economic shift has created a fascinating reality where top tier college athletes pull in staggering compensation packages that rival or exceed professional pay scales.

For the current campaign, at least four college quarterbacks are projected to rake in more than $4 million via NIL valuations , a threshold that only two rookies in the entire NFL class, Mendoza and Simpson ( $4.62 million ), manage to surpass.

The collegiate leaderboard is headlined by Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah , who commands the highest valuation in the entire NCAA at a massive $6.5 million .

Right behind him sit Oregon's Dante Moore at $5 million , Ole Miss standout Trinidad Chambliss at $5 million , LSU's Sam Leavitt at $4.5 million , and Indiana's Josh Hoover rounding out the top five at $4 million .

In stark contrast, once past the top two spots in the NFL draft, rookie compensation drops off sharply; players like Carson Beck ( $1.35 million ), Drew Allar ( $1.29 million ), and Cade Klubnik ( $1.19 million ) populate the next tier of professional arrivals.

Looking at these staggering financial comparisons, it feels surreal to imagine telling a sports fan a decade ago that amateur college players would routinely out-earn mid-round draft picks before ever stepping foot in an official NFL game.

articles.title: Bill Belichick is forced to step up in Dublin and activates an emergency plan for UNC against TCU
articles.standfirst: With his son still sidelined, the veteran coach assumes a critical role in North Carolina’s season opener
articles.summary: With his son still sidelined, the veteran coach assumes a critical role in North Carolina’s season opener
articles.body:
Bill Belichick was handed an unexpected responsibility as North Carolina opened its 2026 season against TCU in Dublin.

With defensive coordinator Steve Belichick still away from the program on medical leave, the veteran head coach called the Tar Heels’ defensive plays himself.

The development, reported by ESPN’s Pete Thamel shortly before kickoff, changes what UNC had previously described as a collective approach to handling Steve’s absence.

Steve Belichick wasn’t with the team in Ireland, leaving his father to assume a role that’s familiar territory for one of football’s most accomplished defensive minds.

Steve was placed on medical leave Aug. 6, with Bill declining to discuss the circumstances or provide a potential return date.

The coach said at the time that the program hoped to have his son back as soon as possible. Weeks later, there’s still no public timetable, and UNC has now reached its first game without its defensive coordinator.

The timing couldn’t be more significant. TCU handed Belichick a brutal introduction to college football last season, racing from an early deficit to a 48-14 victory.

The Horned Frogs produced 542 yards, ran for 258 and capitalized heavily on UNC turnovers. That result remains an obvious measuring stick for a Tar Heels team hoping to prove that last year’s 4-8 campaign was an aberration rather than the beginning of a larger problem.

As a result, Belichick was forced to put his defensive expertise directly into action against a TCU offense that has undergone changes of its own.

Gordon Sammis is taking over as offensive coordinator, while Jaden Craig is expected to lead the Horned Frogs at quarterback. That creates some uncertainty, but TCU’s offensive potential still presents a significant challenge.

Belichick faces pressure from every direction

The defensive situation is only one piece of UNC’s complicated offseason. General manager Michael Lombardi has also been on leave, while Belichick enters his second season under considerable scrutiny after an underwhelming debut.

The Tar Heels averaged just 19.2 points per game in 2025, ranking near the bottom nationally. That offensive ineffectiveness helped produce a disappointing 4-8 record, putting greater pressure on the program to show meaningful progress immediately.

UNC has attempted to address the quarterback position by bringing in Wisconsin transfer Billy Edwards Jr. The signal-caller is expected to provide a spark after the Tar Heels struggled to consistently generate offense last season.

His ability to protect the football and create scoring opportunities could prove crucial as UNC attempts to turn around its fortunes.

The defense also has to overcome personnel losses, making Steve Belichick’s absence even more significant. Several important contributors departed during the offseason, leaving Bill with less margin for error as he tries to establish a more reliable unit.

After last year’s 48-14 defeat, TCU provides a particularly difficult measuring stick. With his son unavailable and expectations already building, Bill Belichick now has to take command when his program needs him most.

articles.title: Bill Belichick gets revenge one year after TCU humiliated him in disastrous college debut
articles.standfirst: The 74-year-old coach returned to face the team that started his nightmare at North Carolina and this time almost everything was different
articles.summary: The 74-year-old coach returned to face the team that started his nightmare at North Carolina and this time almost everything was different
articles.body:
B ill Belichick couldn't have asked for a better way to begin his second season at North Carolina. The Tar Heels beat TCU 15-10 on Saturday in Dublin, giving the 74-year-old coach his first victory of the new season after his defense completely shut down the Horned Frogs in the second half.

It wasn't pretty and it wasn't easy, but when it was over, Belichick was 1-0. And the opponent made this one mean a little more.

One year later, Bill Belichick finally had his answer

Exactly one year earlier, TCU had welcomed the six-time Super Bowl champion to college football in the worst possible way. Belichick's highly anticipated North Carolina debut ended in a brutal 48-14 loss, and the Tar Heels eventually finished his first season 4-8.

This time, even with North Carolina leading 12-10 at halftime, Belichick wasn't interested in talking. An ESPN reporter tried to stop him as he headed toward the locker room and eventually stepped directly into his path.

Belichick briefly slowed down, moved around her and kept walking without saying a word.

By the end of the game, his mood looked very different. When North Carolina was awarded an automatic first down that effectively clinched the victory, Belichick enthusiastically threw his arm forward to make the first-down signal himself.

The normally stone-faced coach smiled as he celebrated from the sideline, knowing his team was finally about to finish the job.

North Carolina's defense didn't allow TCU to score a single point in the second half, a major change from the unit that was overwhelmed by the Horned Frogs a year ago. TCU was also stopped on all three of its fourth-down attempts, while the Tar Heels committed just two penalties for 15 yards compared with TCU's 10 for 85. It wasn't a dominant offensive performance, but it was a much more disciplined team when it mattered.

Belichick now gets a week off before North Carolina returns home to face East Tennessee State on Sept. 12 at Kenan Stadium. But the first real test of how much this team has changed comes one week later, when the Tar Heels travel to face Clemson on Sept. 19. Notre Dame follows in Chapel Hill on Oct. 3, with ACC games against Pitt, Duke, Syracuse and Miami waiting later in October.

For now, Belichick gets to leave Dublin 1-0. A year after TCU gave him a brutal introduction to college football , his second season couldn't have started much better.

articles.title: MicahJo Barnett Cause of Death: Division II college football player tragically passes away mid-game
articles.standfirst: William Jewell College confirmed the news following a game that Barnett took part in on Saturday.
articles.summary: William Jewell College confirmed the news following a game that Barnett took part in on Saturday.
articles.body:
Saturday was supposed to be a special day for all of college football. It marked the beginning of the 2026 season. But tragedy struck midway through the day that sent shockwaves throughout the college football world.

MicahJo Barnett , a running back for Division II William Jewell College in Missouri, tragically passed away during the team's game against Fort Lewis College . Barnett's death was confirmed by the school about two hours after the game was stopped due to Barnett experiencing a "medical emergency" on the sidelines .

MicahJo Barnett experienced "seizure like symptoms" before untimely death

Local Kansas City journalist Harold R. Kuntz reported that Barnett " suffered seizure like symptoms ". EMS responders attended to Barnett, on the field, and he was then transported by ambulance to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead. There still isn't an official cause of death .

Barnett had scored a one-yard touchdown for Jewell earlier in the game . He was a junior and a business administration major . Some of his teammates spoke to local media after the events unfolded, and they tried to keep their heads held high in honor of Barnett.

Barnett was born in Shawnee Mission, Kansas and had six siblings. He earned Academic All-Great Lakes Valley Conference honors last season.

articles.title: What is the longest winning streak in college football? The current NCAAF record
articles.standfirst: Oklahoma's 47-game run still stands alone in Division I history.
articles.summary: Oklahoma's 47-game run still stands alone in Division I history.
articles.body:
The longest winning streak in NCAA Division I college football history still belongs to Oklahoma, whose remarkable run stretched across five seasons in the 1950s.

The Sooners won 47 consecutive games between 1953 and 1957, a record that has survived every modern dynasty that followed.

Oklahoma's streak finally ended against Notre Dame in 1957 , but no FBS program has managed to reach 40 consecutive victories since.

The closest challenge came from Washington, which won 40 straight games between 1908 and 1914 before its streak ended against Oregon State.

Oklahoma's 47-game streak remains the benchmark

The scale of Oklahoma's achievement becomes clearer when compared with other dominant programs.

Toledo put together 35 straight wins between 1969 and 1971, while Miami reached 34 from 2000 to 2002.

USC also recorded a 34 -game streak between 2003 and 2005, although 14 of those victories were later vacated following NCAA sanctions connected to Reggie Bush.

More recently, Georgia won 29 consecutive games between 2021 and 2023 before Alabama ended the run.

Clemson also reached 29 victories across 2018 and 2019, with LSU ending that streak in the College Football Playoff National Championship.

The modern era has produced several huge runs

Alabama won 26 consecutive games between 2015 and 2016, while UCF reached 25 from 2017 to 2018.

Florida State also managed 29 straight victories from 2012 through 2014.

Oklahoma itself appears more than once among the longest streaks in history. Before its record 47 -game run, the Sooners won 31 consecutive games between 1948 and 1950 and later added another 28-game streak from 1973 to 1975.

The FCS record is separate.

North Dakota State holds that mark with 39 consecutive victories between 2017 and 2021, while the Bison also previously produced a 33-game winning streak from 2012 to 2014.

But when discussing the overall NCAA Division I record, Oklahoma remains untouched.

Nearly seven decades after the Sooners reached 47 straight wins, college football is still waiting for another team capable of matching it.

articles.title: The real reason Bill Belichick might never coach in NFL again
articles.standfirst: Legendary coach’s “militant” approach would struggle to connect with current generation
articles.summary: Legendary coach’s “militant” approach would struggle to connect with current generation
articles.body:
Bill Belichick has spent much of his career proving that an uncompromising approach can produce championships. Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson believes that same philosophy could now be the very thing preventing the six-time Super Bowl winner from returning to the NFL .

The former Cincinnati Bengals receiver argued that Belichick ’s famously demanding coaching style is increasingly at odds with a league dominated by younger players who expect a different relationship with their coaches.

Speaking on “Nightcap” alongside Shannon Sharpe , Johnson pointed to the generational shift taking place across the NFL and questioned whether Belichick ’s old-school methods would still translate.

“I think it's the coaching style,” Ochocinco said. “I think it's the coaching style. I don't think his coaching style would resonate with today's players. I don't think it would resonate... I don't think players will respond to that extremely well.”

Belichick coached the New England Patriots from 2000 through 2023, building one of the greatest dynasties in professional sports alongside Tom Brady . But after leaving New England and failing to land another NFL job, he eventually moved into college football with North Carolina.

Johnson believes that may reflect a broader change in what NFL organizations now want from their head coaches.

“I think with the younger generation, I think that's why if you look at most of the coaches throughout the NFL and look at the landscape outside of Harbaugh, it's more younger coaches, coaches that the players can actually relate to and understand,” Johnson said.

“That old school style, that militant style of coaching, yeah, I don't think it would go over very well, especially with this generation that is very very sensitive.”

Sharpe had raised the contrast with John Harbaugh , who quickly returned to coaching after the end of his long tenure with the Baltimore Ravens . Belichick’s situation has unfolded differently.

After separating from the Patriots in January 2024, he spent the following NFL season out of coaching before accepting the North Carolina job in December.

His first season in Chapel Hill produced a 4-8 record and significant scrutiny around the program, although Year 2 began more encouragingly with a 15-10 victory over TCU in Ireland.

The TCU result offered Belichick a timely response to critics questioning whether his approach remains effective.

North Carolina held the Horned Frogs scoreless after their opening two drives and produced a disciplined defensive performance that looked much closer to the identity Belichick built during his NFL career.

That doesn't necessarily change Johnson ’s argument. The challenge of managing an NFL locker room is different from developing a college program, and younger head coaches have increasingly become prominent across the league.

Belichick ’s resume guarantees that his football knowledge will never seriously be questioned. Whether another NFL franchise would hand him control of a modern locker room is a different issue.

Ochocinco ’s view is that the game has changed, the players have changed, and Belichick may have to change with them if he ever wants another opportunity in the NFL.

articles.title: Deion Sanders under fire again as critics claim he was never qualified to coach Colorado
articles.standfirst: Breiden Fehoko says Coach Prime’s celebrity helped mask lack of coaching credentials
articles.summary: Former NFL player Breiden Fehoko says Coach Prime’s celebrity helped mask a lack of traditional coaching credentials
articles.body:
Deion Sanders has never followed a conventional coaching path, and that was part of what made Colorado’s decision to hire him so compelling. Breiden Fehoko now argues it should have been a warning sign instead.

The former NFL defensive lineman has intensified his criticism of Sanders , saying Colorado prioritized celebrity, recruiting power and personality over the kind of coaching background normally associated with a major college football job.

“I know he was never qualified to take the Colorado job,” Fehoko said on The Breiden Fehoko Show.

“He had no FBS coaching experience before Colorado. He went from coaching at Jackson State, who was a FCS school, directly to a Power Five program. We have never seen that type of jump before in the history of college sports.”

Fehoko also pointed to Sanders ’ lack of experience as a traditional college coordinator. That criticism comes at a pivotal point in Sanders’ tenure.

Colorado enters another season after going 3-9 in 2025, a sharp reversal from the 9-4 campaign that had appeared to validate much of the optimism surrounding Coach Prime .

Colorado chose star power over coaching pedigree

Colorado was in desperate need of a reset when Sanders arrived in December 2022.

The Buffaloes had just finished 1-11, were struggling for national relevance and needed a hire capable of generating immediate attention. Sanders certainly did that.

He had gone 27-6 at Jackson State , won consecutive SWAC titles and established himself as one of the most recognizable figures in college football recruiting. Fehoko believes Colorado confused that impact with qualification.

“When I look at Colorado, they hired a phenomenon instead of hiring a coach,” he said.

“They hired somebody who had aura and a resume instead of getting somebody who was qualified to lead men and restore Colorado to where people and the true fans of Boulder wanted to be.”

Sanders has already acknowledged mistakes of his own, particularly when it came to replacing his son Shedeur at quarterback.

“I made a big mistake, man,” Sanders told ESPN this summer. “You got to understand it. I’ve coached my son my whole entire life. So everything was like, compared to that. It’s hard to get.”

Criticism goes back years

His latest comments also come with personal history attached.

Fehoko recently described meeting Sanders when he was 17 at the Under Armour All-American game and asking his childhood idol for a picture and advice.

“I said, ‘Man, Deion, I’m a big fan of you,’” Fehoko recalled. According to him, Sanders simply replied: “Hey, man. Move along.”

Fehoko said the encounter permanently changed his opinion of Sanders , but his current argument is ultimately about results and credentials rather than one old interaction.

Colorado now faces another important season with a rebuilt roster, new coordinators and growing pressure to prove 2024 was more than a temporary breakthrough.
